question.text: Which of the following best describes a zero coupon bond?

answer.text: A bond that pays coupons semi-annually at a floating rate
A bond that does not pay periodic interest and is issued at a discount to face value
A bond that pays interest only at the time of maturity in a lump sum
A bond with zero face value issued at par

explanation.text: The Logic: The essential feature of a zero coupon bond per the workbook is the absence of periodic interest payments. They are commonly issued at a discount to face value, with the implied interest being the difference between the discounted issue price and the face value received at maturity. The workbook also notes that some zero coupon bonds may be issued at par and redeemed with interest at a premium. The Trap: Option A describes a floating-rate coupon bond, which still has periodic coupons. Option C describes a deferred-interest bond with a single interest payout at maturity, which is a distinct structure. Option D wrongly suggests zero face value rather than zero coupons. Note: Option C overlaps somewhat with par-issue / premium-redemption zero coupon bond cases. The defining feature being tested here is the absence of periodic interest, which is what makes Option B the best answer.
